## Summary

Biphenyl-4-carboxylic acid is esterified with methanol. This is sample data; the quantities are not experimentally verified.

## Reagents

| Reagent | CAS | MW (g/mol) | Amount | mmol | Equiv |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Biphenyl-4-carboxylic acid | 92-92-2 | 198.22 | 1.982 g | 10 | 1.0 |
| Sulfuric acid | 7664-93-9 | 98.07 | 0.1 mL | cat. | cat. |
| Methanol | 67-56-1 | 32.04 | 30 mL | – | – |

## Procedure

1. Place biphenyl-4-carboxylic acid in a flask with methanol.
2. Carefully add sulfuric acid while stirring.
3. Fit a reflux condenser open to the atmosphere.
4. Heat the mixture at reflux for 2 hours.
5. Allow the mixture to cool to room temperature.
6. Add water slowly with stirring and cool the mixture in ice.

## Workup and Purification

Collect the precipitated methyl ester by suction filtration, wash with cold water and dry. Expected yield: 1.49 g (7.00 mmol, 70 %).

## Characterization

White crystals; expected IR ester C=O absorption near 1720 cm⁻¹ and ¹H NMR methoxy singlet near δ 3.9.

## Notes

1. Add the acid carefully to the stirred mixture.
2. Keep ignition sources away from methanol vapour.
3. Cool fully to improve crystallisation.

## Hazards and Waste Disposal

Biphenyl-4-carboxylic acid: may irritate skin and eyes; Sulfuric acid: causes severe burns and eye damage; Methanol: highly flammable and toxic; causes organ damage; Methyl biphenyl-4-carboxylate: may irritate skin and eyes. Work in a fume hood; wear gloves and eye protection. Collect the acidic methanolic filtrate as labelled acidic organic waste.

## References

1. Furniss, B. S.; Hannaford, A. J.; Smith, P. W. G.; Tatchell, A. R. Vogel's Textbook of Practical Organic Chemistry, 5th ed.; Longman: Harlow, 1989.
